neighbours.label: calcium-nutrition context: positions where 'calcium' is the expected next word or referent (after calcium / bones / dairy have come up)
fire: Calcium is vital for teenagers, yet many of them do not get enough of it from their meals.
Dairy foods such as cheese are rich in calcium, and fortified juices provide it as well.
Because her bones were thinning, the doctor told her to take calcium tablets with vitamin D every morning.
Calcium builds strong teeth, so dentists advise children to eat foods that contain plenty of it.
Without enough calcium in the diet, the body draws the mineral out of the skeleton.
Sardines and kale supply calcium, which the body stores mainly in the bones and teeth.
Women over fifty are often advised to increase their calcium intake to slow bone loss.
The label says one glass of milk gives a third of the calcium an adult needs each day.
quiet: Iron is vital for teenagers, yet many of them do not get enough of it from their meals.
Citrus fruits such as oranges are rich in vitamin C, and fortified cereals provide it as well.
Because her blood count was low, the doctor told her to take iron tablets with orange juice every morning.
Fibre aids digestion, so doctors advise children to eat foods that contain plenty of it.
Without enough potassium in the diet, the muscles cramp and the heart may beat unevenly.
Lentils and beef supply iron, which the body uses mainly to carry oxygen in the blood.
Runners over fifty are often advised to increase their protein intake to slow muscle loss.
The label says one bowl of lentils gives a third of the protein an adult needs each day.

notes: Card: the token just before 'calcium' in five languages ('enough', 'taking', 'of the'); the + pole's direct effect promotes ' calcium'/' Ca', so this late-layer pole pushes against the word it anticipates. Probes: 0.60 and 0.42 (peak at the end of calcium sentences), 'milligrams of [it]' 0.53; iron versions 0.00-0.01, 'enough sleep' 0.01; but dairy alone leaks ('sources of' after milk and yogurt 0.27, 'low in dairy' 0.21).
